speech.text: Two animals that figured out a way to save us. In 1998, Joanne Altman collapsed from a heart attack. Her husband was out fishing. Nobody could hear her crying for help. The only one around was Lulu, her adopted pot -bellied pig. She looked at Joanne nervously, whining like she was crying. Then, she tried to squeeze through the doggy door, but her body was so big that it actually tore her belly open. She busted through the fence, leaving the yard she had never left by herself before. She ran straight out to the main road and laid down right in the middle of it. Cars honked and swerved. A few people stopped but didn't dare to get out. Lulu went back, squeezed through the little door, checked on Joanne, and then ran right back out to the road. For 45 minutes, she kept running back and forth, the wound on her belly tore wider and wider, but she never stopped until one guy worried about her injuries finally followed her. Even crazier is the story from 2017. Nan Hauser was diving with two humpback whales in the Cook Islands when one of them suddenly charged right at her. It pushed her from below with its head, then used its massive fin to tuck her right up against its body. Nan totally panicked and tried to struggle free, but the whale wouldn't let her go. It pushed her onto its back and lifted her completely out of the water. At that exact moment, she saw a 15 -foot tiger shark right behind her, charging fast. The other whale was swimming right beside them, constantly slapping its tail hard against the water. That's when Nan realized. The two whales were using their own bodies to shield her.
